overview: This Senate resolution congratulates Northwest Mississippi Community College on its 100th anniversary. The school began college-level classes on September 7, 1926, grew out of a county agricultural high school founded in 1915, and took its current name in 1988. It now serves an 11-county area of North Mississippi from its main campus in Senatobia and several other sites, with more than 8,000 students a year. The resolution praises its academic, job-training, health sciences and athletic programs and asks that copies be sent to college leaders. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on August 5, 2026.
for: Supporters say the college has widened access to higher education and job training across North Mississippi for a century and deserves national recognition.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it changes no law and provides no funding.
